findings.title: Visible signs before an unsettled majority
findings.claim: Visible signs stand before a human collective whose perceptual root field sharpens the irony that numerical predominance does not become inward trust.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are āyātu, akthara, al-nāsi, and yuʾminūna. The construct relation, adversative truth contrast, and final negation independently connect visible indicators, the human majority, perception, and absent trust.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a collective that can stand among signs and yet fail to take them into an inward trust response.
findings.containment: The ordinary meanings remain signs, most people, and non-belief. The perception branch is attributed root resonance; al-nāsi still names humans and is not itself a verb of seeing.

epistemic.reason: The QAC surface roots and focus positions are supplied, but the root roles and changed reading are from a legacy_unbound HFT trace; the perception branch is also qualified.
